title: True / False / Not Given
title_target: Reading — identifying information & the writer's views
goal: Membedakan FALSE dari NOT GIVEN dengan pasti, menemukan kalimat sumber tiap pernyataan dalam waktu kurang dari satu menit, dan tidak terjebak kata yang kebetulan sama.
bekal: menjelaskan kenapa pernyataan itu FALSE atau NOT GIVEN dengan menunjuk kalimatnya
mengenali lima bentuk pengecoh yang dipakai penulis soal
mengerjakan 13 soal passage ini dalam 20 menit

sections.title: Kenapa tipe soal ini menjatuhkan orang pintar

blocks.text: *True/False/Not Given* (TFNG) adalah tipe soal Reading yang paling sering muncul dan paling sering salah dijawab — bukan oleh yang lemah bahasa Inggrisnya, justru oleh yang kuat. Alasannya: pembaca yang baik terbiasa **menyimpulkan**. Ia membaca "the council installed 40 hives on public rooftops" dan otomatis menyimpulkan "jadi kota itu mendukung lebah". Di IELTS, kesimpulan itu belum tentu ada di teks, dan pernyataan yang tidak ada di teks jawabannya **NOT GIVEN**, sepintar apa pun kesimpulannya.

blocks.title: Tiga definisi yang harus kamu hafal persis
items: **TRUE** — teks mengatakan hal yang SAMA dengan pernyataan, biasanya dengan kata yang berbeda (paraphrase).
**FALSE** — teks mengatakan hal yang BERTENTANGAN dengan pernyataan. Kalau pernyataan benar, teksnya jadi salah. Keduanya tidak bisa benar bersamaan.
**NOT GIVEN** — teks TIDAK MEMBAHAS hal itu. Pernyataan bisa benar di dunia nyata, bisa masuk akal, bisa kamu simpulkan — tetap NOT GIVEN kalau tidak tertulis.

blocks.text: Uji cepat untuk FALSE vs NOT GIVEN: tanyakan *"Apakah teks ini bisa dipakai untuk MEMBANTAH pernyataan itu?"* Kalau bisa, FALSE. Kalau teksnya diam soal itu, NOT GIVEN. Pernyataan "Urban beekeeping began in Paris" ketika teks berkata "the first rooftop hives appeared in Paris": TRUE. Ketika teks berkata "the first rooftop hives appeared in New York": FALSE — teks membantah. Ketika teks hanya berkata "rooftop hives are now common in Paris": NOT GIVEN — teks tidak bilang di mana mulainya.

Versi kembarannya, **YES/NO/NOT GIVEN**, dipakai kalau passage berisi **pendapat penulis** (opini, argumen, klaim), bukan fakta. Cara kerjanya sama persis; hanya kata jawabannya yang berbeda, dan itu penting: menulis TRUE di soal YES/NO dinilai **salah** walaupun maksudmu benar. Baca instruksinya.

sections.title: Strategi: lima langkah, satu menit per soal

items: **Baca pernyataannya dulu, bukan passage-nya.** Soal TFNG mengikuti URUTAN passage — jawaban soal 3 ada setelah jawaban soal 2. Ini alat navigasi gratis.

**Garis bawahi kata kunci yang tidak bisa diparafrase**: nama, angka, tahun, tempat, istilah teknis. Kata-kata inilah yang kamu *scan* di teks. Kata umum (important, people, change) hampir pasti ditulis dengan kata lain.
**Temukan kalimat sumbernya**, lalu baca kalimat itu **dan satu kalimat sebelum-sesudahnya** dengan teliti. Jangan menjawab dari ingatan.

**Bandingkan pernyataan dengan kalimat sumber satu bagian demi satu bagian**: subjeknya sama? kata kerjanya sama? angkanya sama? kata pembatasnya (*all, only, mainly, first, always*) sama? Satu bagian yang bertentangan = FALSE. Satu bagian yang tidak disebut = NOT GIVEN.
**Kalau 90 detik tidak ketemu kalimat sumbernya, tulis NOT GIVEN dan lanjut.** Secara statistik, pernyataan yang tidak bisa kamu temukan sumbernya kemungkinan besar memang tidak ada.

blocks.title: Lima pengecoh favorit penulis soal
items: **Kata pembatas diganti.** Teks: *most* students → soal: *all* students. FALSE.
**Pelaku ditukar.** Teks: *the government funded* the project → soal: *a private company funded*. FALSE.
**Sebab-akibat dikarang.** Teks menyebut A dan B berdampingan → soal: *A caused B*. Biasanya NOT GIVEN.
**Perbandingan ditambahkan.** Teks: *the method is popular* → soal: *the method is more popular than X*. NOT GIVEN, kecuali teksnya membandingkan.
**Kata yang sama, makna berbeda.** Soal memakai kata yang persis ada di teks supaya kamu merasa "ketemu", padahal kalimatnya membahas hal lain. Selalu baca seluruh kalimat sumbernya.

blocks.text: Kalimat sumber: *"Although the scheme was launched by the city council in 2015, its running costs have been met almost entirely by corporate sponsors since 2018."*

head: Pernyataan
Jawaban
Kenapa
rows: The scheme was started by the local authority.
TRUE
*launched by the city council* = *started by the local authority*. Paraphrase penuh, maknanya sama.
Corporate sponsors have paid for the scheme since it began.
FALSE
Teks: sponsor membayar *since 2018*, sedangkan mulainya 2015. Bertentangan.
Corporate sponsors receive tax benefits for their support.
NOT GIVEN
Teks tidak menyebut *tax* atau imbalan apa pun. Masuk akal, tapi tidak tertulis.
The council no longer contributes anything to the running costs.
NOT GIVEN
*Almost entirely* berarti ada sisa kecil yang mungkin dari council, mungkin dari pihak lain. Teks tidak mengatakan council berhenti sama sekali — tidak bisa dibantah, tidak bisa dibenarkan.

blocks.text: Perhatikan baris terakhir: banyak siswa menjawab FALSE karena "kan sponsor yang bayar". Tapi *almost entirely* justru menyisakan celah, dan teks tidak mengisi celah itu. Inilah bedanya membaca **apa yang tertulis** dengan membaca **apa yang masuk akal**.

Kerjakan Latihan 1–3 di bawah dari passage ini. Ukur waktumu: target **20 menit** untuk membaca dan menjawab 13 soal. Di reader, ketuk kata yang tidak kamu kenal untuk mendengar dan melihat artinya — tapi coba dulu tanpa itu, seperti di ruang ujian.

blocks.title: The Quiet Rise of Urban Beekeeping

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: When the first beehives appeared on the roof of the Paris Opera House in the early 1980s, they were regarded as an eccentric hobby of one of the building's technicians. Four decades later, hives sit on the rooftops of banks, hotels, department stores and government offices in almost every major European city, and urban beekeeping has become a small industry with its own suppliers, training courses and, inevitably, its own critics. The bees, it turns out, have taken to city life rather better than anyone expected.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The reasons are not obvious. Cities are noisy, polluted and covered in concrete, none of which sounds attractive to an insect that lives on flowers. Yet several studies conducted in London, Berlin and Paris between 2010 and 2019 found that urban colonies produced, on average, more honey per hive than their rural counterparts, and that they survived the winter in greater numbers. The explanation lies in what has happened to the countryside. Modern farmland is dominated by a handful of crops that flower briefly and simultaneously; for the rest of the year there is little for a bee to eat. Cities, by contrast, contain parks, gardens, railway embankments, street trees and window boxes planted with hundreds of different species, which between them flower from early spring to late autumn. Urban areas are also, on the whole, slightly warmer than the surrounding land, which extends the foraging season. And city gardeners use far fewer pesticides than commercial farmers.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Local authorities were quick to see the appeal. A rooftop hive costs little, requires no planning permission in most cities, and produces a photograph of a smiling official in a bee suit that newspapers are reliably happy to print. Between 2012 and 2018 the number of registered hives in London more than doubled, from around 3,500 to over 7,500, and Paris reported a similar increase. Corporate sponsors followed: a hive on the roof of a head office became a convenient way of demonstrating environmental credentials without altering anything the company actually did.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: It is at this point that the critics enter. Honeybees, they point out, are not wild animals in need of protection; they are livestock, managed by humans, and their numbers worldwide have been rising for decades. The insects that are genuinely in trouble are wild bees – bumblebees, solitary bees and the hundreds of other species that receive no attention from sponsors because they produce no honey and pose for no photographs. A 2020 survey led by the ecologist Dr Marta Villalba estimated that central London now supports roughly ten times more honeybee colonies than its available flowers can comfortably feed. Where that happens, the honeybees, which forage in large numbers and over long distances, simply out-compete their wild relatives for nectar and pollen. The rooftop hive, installed to help the bees, may be harming the ones that need help most.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Beekeepers dispute the scale of the problem, though not its existence. They argue that the shortage is not of bees but of flowers, and that the sensible response is to plant more rather than to keep fewer hives. Several cities have begun to do exactly that. Since 2019, new hives in central Paris have been permitted only if the applicant can show that an equivalent area of flowering plants has been added nearby, and a number of British councils have replaced closely mown grass in parks with wildflower meadows, which cost less to maintain and support many more insects.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Whether urban beekeeping is good for cities therefore depends, rather unhelpfully, on how it is done. A single well-managed hive in a district with plenty of green space almost certainly does no harm, and the keeper who tends it will notice – and probably start to care about – the flowers, weather and wildlife of a place that most residents walk through without seeing. Fifty hives on the roofs of neighbouring office blocks, installed for the sake of a press release, are another matter. The bees themselves, of course, are indifferent to the argument. They will go on doing what they have always done, which is to find whatever is flowering within three kilometres and bring it home.

exercises.prompt: Questions 1–7. Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage? Write TRUE if the statement agrees with the information, FALSE if the statement contradicts the information, NOT GIVEN if there is no information on this.
items: The first rooftop hives in Paris were set up by the management of the Opera House. ____
Studies found that city bees produced more honey than bees kept in the countryside. ____
Farmland provides bees with food for only a short part of the year. ____
Setting up a rooftop hive usually requires official approval from the city. ____
The number of registered hives in London rose more quickly than in Paris. ____
Honeybee numbers around the world have been falling. ____
Wild bee species receive little attention because they are not commercially useful. ____

exercises.prompt: Questions 8–10. Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in paragraphs E and F? Write YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer, NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
items: Beekeepers accept that there is some competition between honeybees and wild bees. ____
Wildflower meadows are more expensive for councils to look after than mown grass. ____
A large group of hives installed mainly for publicity is likely to be harmful. ____

exercises.prompt: Questions 11–13. Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage for each answer.
items: Urban areas tend to be ____ than the countryside around them, so bees can collect food for longer.
According to a 2020 survey, central London has about ____ as many honeybee colonies as its flowers can support.
In Paris, permission for a new hive now depends on planting an equivalent area of ____ close by.

answers: FALSE — TRUE — TRUE — FALSE — NOT GIVEN — FALSE — TRUE

head: No
Jawaban
Kalimat sumber & alasan
rows: FALSE
Par. A: *an eccentric hobby of one of the building's technicians*. Yang memasang teknisi, bukan manajemen. Pelaku ditukar → bertentangan.
TRUE
Par. B: *urban colonies produced, on average, more honey per hive than their rural counterparts*. *Rural counterparts* = *bees kept in the countryside*.
TRUE
Par. B: *crops that flower briefly and simultaneously; for the rest of the year there is little for a bee to eat*. Paraphrase: makanan hanya tersedia sebentar.
FALSE
Par. C: *requires no planning permission in most cities*. Pernyataan bilang *usually requires* — kebalikan persis dari *in most cities* tidak perlu.
NOT GIVEN
Par. C menyebut London *more than doubled* dan Paris *a similar increase*. Tidak ada perbandingan mana yang LEBIH cepat. Pengecoh: perbandingan ditambahkan.
FALSE
Par. D: *their numbers worldwide have been rising for decades*. *Falling* bertentangan langsung dengan *rising*.
TRUE
Par. D: *receive no attention from sponsors because they produce no honey and pose for no photographs* = tidak bernilai komersial.
YES
Par. E: *Beekeepers dispute the scale of the problem, though not its existence*. Mereka mengakui masalahnya ADA, hanya memperdebatkan besarnya.
NO
Par. E: wildflower meadows *cost less to maintain*. Pernyataan bilang *more expensive* — penulis mengklaim sebaliknya.
YES

Par. F: *Fifty hives … installed for the sake of a press release, are another matter* — kontras dengan *almost certainly does no harm*. Penulis menyiratkan itu merugikan; dalam YES/NO, sikap penulis yang jelas tersirat dihitung.
warmer
Par. B: *slightly warmer than the surrounding land, which extends the foraging season*. Bentuk katanya harus persis dari teks: *warmer*, bukan *warm*.
ten times
Par. D: *roughly ten times more honeybee colonies than its available flowers can comfortably feed*. Dua kata, sesuai batas.
flowering plants
Par. E: *an equivalent area of flowering plants has been added nearby*. *Flowers* saja tidak diterima karena teksnya *flowering plants* dan soal minta kata dari passage.

blocks.title: Yang perlu dicatat dari passage ini
items: Soal 5 dan 10 adalah dua sisi mata uang yang sama: di soal 5, perbandingan yang TIDAK ada di teks → NOT GIVEN. Di soal 10, sikap penulis yang jelas dari kontras kalimatnya → YES. Bedanya: soal 5 menanyakan FAKTA (angka), soal 10 menanyakan PENDAPAT, dan pendapat boleh tersirat dari cara penulis menyusun kalimatnya.
Soal 11–13 memakai batas *NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER*. Jawaban tiga kata otomatis salah walaupun maknanya benar. Hitung katamu sebelum menulis.
